title: Cross-functional roadmap sync prep - Feb 2026 (Asha personal notes)
summary: Prep notes for cross-functional roadmap alignment sync focused on Optimize, Serving Runtime improvements, and Private deployment schedule. Personal scratchpad with key questions, risks, and proposed action items.
content:
Context:
- Weekly cross-functional roadmap sync between Product, Eng (serving runtime + infra), and Applied ML. Primary goal: align on launch timing and resource needs for Q2 items (Optimize recommendations, kernel selection work, Private deployment parity features).

Meeting goals (what I want to get out of the sync):
1) Confirm target milestones for Optimize MVP (recommendation engine + UI suggestions) and list dependencies.
2) Validate priority of serving-runtime kernel selection work vs. autoscaling improvements given limited eng capacity.
3) Agree on a pragmatic feature subset for Private deployments v1 that we can commit to for early enterprise customers.
4) Identify clear owners and due dates for unresolved dependencies (QA, infra quotas, compliance review).

Agenda (30-45 min):
- 5m: Quick status round (Product, Eng, Applied ML) - 1 slide each
- 8m: Optimize MVP scope & risks (Product + Applied ML)
- 10m: Serving runtime priorities (kernel selection, batching, KV cache ergonomics) (Eng)
- 8m: Private deployment parity checklist and rollouts (Product + Infra + Sec)
- 4m: Decisions & action items recap

Prep notes / facts to bring:
- Optimize: internal evals show 18-22% cost savings on average for our test prompt sets when using the suggested batching+cache config. Need to confirm sample size and variance before we claim in docs. (See Confluence page linked).
- Kernel selection: two approaches on table - adaptive kernel selector (more infra work, better long-term perf) vs. static heuristics tuned per model family (less infra, faster delivery). Perf numbers: adaptive improves p95 by ~15% on long-contexts in lab, but requires changes to runtime config API and can complicate canary rollouts.
- Private deployments: customers expect parity on observability (token-level cost breakdown) and rollout controls. We currently have scoped console hooks but not the same retention guarantees.

Key questions to raise / decide in sync:
- Does Product accept shipping Optimize MVP without adaptive kernel selector integrated (i.e., provide recommendations that work with static heuristics initially)? Pros: faster time-to-market. Cons: may underperform for some long-context workloads.
- Prioritization: if eng capacity is limited, should we shift some work from kernel-selection into improving autoscaler stability (targeting better utilization on Dedicated pools) which has more immediate cost impact for customers?
- Private parity: which observability features are MUST vs NICE-TO-HAVE for GA? I propose MUST = token-level cost breakouts, per-route dashboards, and audit log export. NICE = extended retention and custom alerting tiers.

Data & metrics to cite during discussion:
- p95 generation latency baseline (hosted v2 models): 420ms median p95 across prod tests for 2k tokens workload. (Source: internal perf dashboard, note: sample skewed to small bursts)
- Cost impact: Optimize eval harness suggests median token cost reduction 20% on web-search workload; variance +/- 8%.
- Dedicated utilization: autopilot currently averages 62% GPU utilization in demo clusters; target 75-80% for efficiency improvements.

Risks / Blockers:
- Kernel selector requires infra changes that may block some canary workflows (risk: rollback complexity).
- Private deployment compliance review timeline not confirmed with legal (ask: can security carve out a fast-path for early pilot customers?).
- QA capacity: need additional SRE/QA cycles to validate rolling updates with new kernel selection heuristics.

Proposed decisions (for group to agree on):
1) Ship Optimize MVP with static heuristics + clear roadmap item to integrate adaptive selector in +2 sprints.
2) Re-prioritize 2 engineer-weeks from kernel selection to autoscaler stability if Product accepts a slight delay on long-context perf.
3) Private GA: require the MUST observability items; defer extended retention to a follow-up milestone.

Action items (draft - to review & confirm owners in sync):
- Asha (Product): finalize Optimize MVP feature list and marketing language by 2026-02-22. Link PR for docs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/102.
- Raj (Eng - runtime): produce a short tech-note comparing adaptive vs static kernel approaches with rollout/rollback plan by 2026-02-25. (JIRA: RDWD-842).
- Maya (Applied ML): expand eval set for Optimize to include 3 additional customer workloads and push results to Confluence by 2026-02-24.
- Dylan (Infra/SRE): estimate QA/SRE cycles needed for kernel-selector testing and autoscaler stability work; propose support plan by 2026-02-23.
- Legal/Security (TBD): confirm fast-path for pilot compliance review or provide expected timeline by 2026-02-26.

Notes to self (personal scratchpad during the meeting):
- If Product pushes for GA messaging, call out variance in cost savings and avoid absolute numbers until we have larger N.
- Emphasize we can ship a conservative Optimize settings UI that surfaces confidence intervals and 'try on sample' to build trust.
- If kernel-selector is blocked, propose a middle ground: static heuristics + telemetry flags so we can experiment in prod without full runtime change.

Follow-up / next steps after sync:
- Circulate meeting notes and updated action-item table within 24 hours.
- Schedule a dedicated 30m deep-dive with runtime + applied-ml to finalize the kernel selector decision (invite: Raj, Dylan, Maya, Asha).
- Add a QA gating ticket to roadmap with clear exit criteria for kernel-selector/autoscaler changes.

Misc references (quick links I might paste in chat during the meeting):
- Confluence: Cross-Functional Roadmap Feb 2026 (linked above)
- JIRA: RDWD-842 (kernel selection), RDWD-799 (Optimize eval harness), RDWD-810 (Private deployment observability)
- GH: serving-runtime PR #456 (kernel selector spike), docs PR #102 (Optimize MVP copy)

End of notes.

(Will tidy and convert into meeting notes doc after the sync - keep this as my scratchpad)
